targetTest: reminds after fifteen elapsed minutes despite a backward wall-clock correction
expected: After an initial warning, the next failure at thirty elapsed seconds is debug. A one-hour backward wall-clock correction does not delay the reminder: at fifteen elapsed minutes the next failure warns. Recovery logs once and a new failure warns as a fresh incident.
actual: The third failure at fifteen elapsed minutes logged debug instead of warn because the committed FailureLog subtracted its previous wall-clock warning timestamp from a wall time moved back one hour. Recovery and the subsequent fresh warning still logged as expected.
semanticAssessment: The final active test blob ec7d605191eedb14e83a47e705e0a323970a3561 compiled and executed exactly one named case against unchanged committed production blobs for failureLog and accountRuntime at HEAD 4f3cbb5dcb21329f519f0bf29c43711ff0062364. Its deepStrictEqual failed only at the elapsed reminder boundary: expected warn, actual debug. The case also asserted initial warning, interval debug, single recovery, and fresh warning. This is the intended product behavior failure, not a build, fixture, runner, or environment failure. The final test helper supplies its forward-only clock under both option names so it compiles against committed RED and the GREEN constructor; the preliminary RED archive used an earlier helper patch.
